detailed_description: The PDF Rotator enables granular manipulation of PDF page orientation through direct modification of page rotation matrices within the PDF document structure. Unlike generic tools that apply uniform transformations, this utility allows precise 90° clockwise, counterclockwise, or 180° rotation at the page level using Adobe Portable Document Format specification-compliant matrix operations. Users require this tool for correcting misaligned scanned documents, optimizing print layouts, adjusting image-heavy PDFs with inconsistent EXIF orientation data, or preparing presentation materials with mixed portrait/landscape content. The backend employs Poppler's rendering engine to parse page objects, applies affine transformations to the PDF's internal coordinate system, and preserves original metadata, annotations, and layer structures during rotation. Batch processing leverages parallelized worker threads to maintain performance with multi-page documents while retaining individual page control through a thumbnail-based interface.
usage_steps: Access the tool via browser and click 'Upload PDF' to select your document (max 100MB) using the drag-and-drop interface
Review pages in the thumbnail grid where red indicators mark orientation inconsistencies based on embedded rotation flags
Click individual page thumbnails or use Shift+Click to select multiple pages requiring adjustment
Choose rotation direction (CW/CCW 90° or 180°) from the context toolbar or use keyboard shortcuts (R/L/X)
Verify changes in the dual-pane preview that highlights transformation matrices before and after rotation
Click 'Download Modified PDF' to generate and save the updated document with preserved OCR layers and bookmark structure
usage_examples: A researcher corrects 180° inverted pages from a two-sided document feeder scan while maintaining original annotation layers
A graphic designer rotates 12 landscape-oriented figures in a 50-page technical report without affecting embedded vector diagrams
An office worker standardizes orientation of 30 mixed-receipt scans with inconsistent mobile camera angles before archiving
A student adjusts a 10-chapter thesis PDF where chapters imported from different sources have conflicting portrait/landscape layouts
